lines.text: Oh that we might begin a new life! How different it would
be, and how much better. No doubt many a time and in
many things we can make a new start by taking a fierce
resolution, and we should do so. But does this always
succeed? And above all, we cannot do this in the most
important matters. For who can silence the voice of con-
science, which reminds us of past guilt? Which of us could
cleanse ourselves of all the stains which sully our past?
Which of us could restore so much that is grievously,
irreparably, damaged in our life and community? For how
many of us is it true that it is now too late!
Does Sunday spell a new beginning for us in these respects
too? We must remember that the Lord's Day is the Day of
the resurrection of Christ; the day on which the new world
of life in the spirit victoriously broke in upon the old world
of sin and death, and so initiated a new beginning for all
who honour the Risen Lord as their Saviour and Master.
"If any one is in Christ he is a new creation; the old has
passed away, behold, the new has come. All this is from God
who through Christ reconciled us to Himself."
It is not in our power to make a new beginning, but God
has made a new beginning for us. And again and again we
can allow this divine initiative to become a reality for us,
we can repeatedly be strengthened and refreshed by it. This
is the very meaning of God's word which each new Sunday
proclaims to us; it warns us that we may and must do this,
that our thoughts should not remain centred on our old
life but on the grace which God bestows on us in Christ.
The bells ring out the message that we are they whose life
He has restored, whom He has reconciled to Himself,
sinners whom He has forgiven, the impure whom He has
made pure. Sunday as the Lord's Day is meant to give us
the assurance that we in all our guilt and weakness belong
even now to the new world, the world of God and of eternal
life. Just as this day is excepted from the course of our work-
ing time which binds us to the old world, so through the
grace of Christ we are lifted out of this world, freed from this
world and from ourselves, in so far as we are still implicated
